text:
Nora Patel: Heads up — customer @AcmeCorp reporting a steady ~6-12% 5xx rate from the hosted API over the last 25m. See sample traces tr-9a3f2c and tr-9a3f2d. Root responses are 502 from edge. Anyone actively triaging?
Raj Singh: I see matching spikes in our metrics. Envoy upstream reset errors rising on us-west frontdoors, ~15:02 -> 15:20 window. Logs show `upstream_reset_before_response_started` and occasional `connection reset by peer`.
Emma Li: Can repro locally against the same frontdoor node with a short curl loop. Posting a small reproducer: 
```bash
for i in {1..30}; do \\curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}\n" -o /dev/null -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -X POST https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"ping","max_tokens":10}'; sleep 0.5; done
```
Emma Li: When I hit the node directly I get intermittent 502s, occasionally 504s. Latency also jumps to ~1.2s on success.
Mike O'Connor: Noted. Can we get the exact frontdoor node IPs/hostnames and a few trace IDs? I'll check oncall routing and upstream NGINX/worker saturation.
Nora Patel: Sample traces: tr-9a3f2c, tr-9a3f2d, tr-9a3f2f. Frontdoor: fd-usw-12a.prod.internal (10.20.11.52). Customer payloads are small single-turn requests — not bulk.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-345, severity: P2. Pinged eng-oncall.
Raj Singh: Quick observation from metrics: keepalive pool usage on that frontdoor jumped ~3x at the start of the window. Connection counts peaked and then succeeded/failed in bursts. Could be h2 stream/keepalive exhaustion.
Emma Li: I captured sample headers from a failed request: 
```
:status: 502
x-envoy-upstream-service-time: 3
server: envoy
x-forwarded-for: 203.0.113.45
x-request-id: tr-9a3f2c
```
Mike O'Connor: Two immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily increase upstream idle timeout and connection pool size for fd-usw-12a to relieve churn, 2) enable the fallback route to dedicated-usw for the tenant to avoid impacted frontdoor nodes. I'll push a short-lived route change (10m) if SRE approves.
Nora Patel: +1 on fallback. Customer is ok with a temporary routing change. Please coordinate.
Raj Singh: I'm tailing envoy logs now and see repeated `RST_STREAM` with code 2 at similar times. Also some TLS renegotiation errors — could be client-side churn combined with pool exhaustion.
Emma Li: Repro steps for support notes: 1) run the curl loop against fd-usw-12a, 2) collect `curl -v` output for failures, 3) paste `x-request-id` into Kibana to gather full upstream traces.
Mike O'Connor: I've prepared a short config diff for the frontdoor pool tweak, requesting SRE approval in #eng-sre. If approved I'll apply and monitor for 15m.
Nora Patel: FYI customer asked for ETA on fix. I'll tell them we have a temporary routing change planned and will confirm in 10m.
Raj Singh: Also adding a throttling rule on client connection bursts for that tenant for now to smooth fanout. That should reduce upstream resets while we investigate root cause.
Emma Li: After 5m post-mitigation check: 502 rate dropped from 9% -> 1.5% on the affected tenant, latency normalized on successful requests. Still seeing a few RSTs but much lower.
Mike O'Connor: Thanks team. Next steps: full postmortem if root cause is frontdoor keepalive leak or TLS churn; otherwise close after 24h stability. I'll leave the temporary route for 30m then roll back if stable.
Nora Patel: Great — I'll update the customer and keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:
Emma Li: Adding a note to support ticket with the curl snippet and `x-request-id`s for the customer so they can share if needed.
sre-bot: INC-2026-345 updated: mitigation applied (route fallback + pool increase). Monitoring metrics.
